title: Delete and rename

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: We do not need `old.txt` any more, and `main.html` should be called `index.html`.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git rm old.txt` deletes the file **and** stages the deletion in one step.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git mv main.html index.html` renames it and stages that too.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: One warning before you start, because this trips up almost everyone.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Not every command is a git command. `git` only handles version control.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Making a folder is a plain shell job: that is `mkdir`, never `git mkdir`.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Make a folder called `archive` first, then do the delete and the rename.

items.text: Make an archive folder (a shell job, not a git job)
Rename main.html to index.html with git
Answer: which of these is not a git command?

hints: One of these four steps is not a git command at all.
Folders are made with the shell command `mkdir`. The delete and rename use `git rm` and `git mv`.
Run `mkdir archive`, then `git rm old.txt`, `git mv main.html index.html`, and `git commit -m "Clean up files"`.
recap: `git rm` deletes and stages in one step; `git mv` renames and stages. Plain file jobs like making a folder use the shell (`mkdir`), not git.

questions.prompt: You need a new folder. Which command makes one?
questions.explanation: `mkdir` is a shell command, not a git one. Git only manages versions of files; the shell manages the files and folders themselves.
